tagline: Gravel roads lead from Winifred to overlooks above the Missouri.
intro: The Missouri Breaks Back Country Byway follows gravel and unimproved roads to overlooks above the Upper Missouri National Wild and Scenic River. Driving time is approximately two to three hours. Visit Montana presents this National Back Country Byway as a journey through rugged country with contrasting scenery and opportunities for solitude.

The route begins at Winifred, a town founded in 1913 at the end of a new Milwaukee Road branch line. Beyond town, the byway closely follows the Nez Perce National Historic Trail toward Deweese Ridge. In 1877, the Nez Perce crossed the Missouri into the Breaks while attempting to escape to Canada.

Begin at Winifred and follow the byway northeast toward Deweese Ridge. The overlooks face a river designated Wild and Scenic in 1976. Across the Breaks, rock outcrops and steep bluffs interrupt grassy plains: the land appears to break away toward the water.

moments.title: Winifred
moments.text: Winifred began where the rails ended. In 1913, a newly built Milwaukee Road branch line reached its terminus here, and the town was founded. A year later, Stafford’s Grocery was built at 201 Main Street. Its native sandstone and decorative details give the early town a material presence: a projecting cornice above a transom of colored prism glass. The building entered the National Register of Historic Places in 2016.

moments.title: Deweese Ridge
moments.text: Between Winifred and Deweese Ridge, the byway closely follows the Nez Perce National Historic Trail. That corridor carries a history of flight. In 1877, the eastbound Nez Perce crossed the Missouri and entered the Breaks in an attempt to escape to Canada. The Cow Island Skirmish took place in the Breaks before the Nez Perce surrendered to the U.S. Army at the Battle of Bear Paw, north of the monument.

moments.title: Fred Robinson Bridge
moments.text: Four steel-girder spans carry the Fred Robinson Bridge across the Missouri between Fergus and Phillips counties. Its construction was controversial, and the name recognizes a forceful supporter: Montana state senator Fred Robinson. The bridge entered the National Register of Historic Places in 2012 as part of a multiple-property submission covering Montana’s steel stringer and steel girder bridges.
moments.notice: Look for the four steel-girder spans over the Missouri.

practical: Winifred: The byway becomes impassable when wet. Check the weather and do not attempt the drive if wet weather threatens. (checked 2026-10-11)
